data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Scabicides & pediculicides_

**Class:** Elemental sulphur in petrolatum (scabicide); also keratolytic and antimicrobial

## Mechanism of action
- Converted to hydrogen sulphide/pentathionic acid on skin → toxic to mites, fungi and bacteria; keratolytic

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Scabies in infants under 2 months and pregnancy (safe, cheap)
- Acne, rosacea, seborrhoeic dermatitis, pityriasis versicolor (with salicylic acid)

## Dose & formulations
- Scabies: 5–10% ointment nightly for 3 nights (wash off before next application), repeat after a week

## Adverse effects
- Messy, malodorous, staining; irritant dermatitis with prolonged use

## Contraindications
- Sulphur sensitivity

## Pregnancy & lactation
Safe — option in pregnancy and infancy.

## Viva points
- Safest scabicide in infants and pregnancy (but messy)

_Sources: Khopkar ch.21 (Precipitated sulfur); Wolverton 4e ch.44. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
